prompt:
Draw a quilter's seam plan drawn in fine pen on graph-free white paper: dots are the seam corners and lines are the stitched seams joining two corners.

Rules you must follow exactly:
- Draw exactly 14 dots. Every dot is a SOLID FILLED circle, clearly fatter than the lines (about five times the line thickness).
- Join dots only with straight stitched lines. EVERY dot must have EXACTLY 3 lines meeting it -- the same number at every single dot, no dot with 2 and no dot with 4.
- Scatter the dots IRREGULARLY. Do NOT arrange them symmetrically: no mirror symmetry, no rosette / mandala / star pattern, no ring of evenly spaced dots, no regular grid.
- Keep it readable: a line must never pass close to a dot it does not end at, two lines meeting at the same dot must leave it in clearly different directions (a wide angle apart), and no line may loop back to the dot it started from.
- Draw it on a PLAIN, evenly coloured background -- no wood grain, no photographic texture, no gradient or shading behind the drawing -- and keep the lines and the dots in one strong colour that clearly contrasts with that background.
- Nothing else in the picture: no text, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no legend, no compass rose, no border decoration.

Count the lines at each dot as you draw, and adjust until every dot has exactly 3 lines.
easy_question: This image was supposed to show a NETWORK DRAWING: several solid round dots joined to each other by lines (the requested subject was: a quilter's seam plan: solid dots joined by straight stitched-seam lines). Ignoring artistic quality and styling, does the image actually show such a dots-and-lines network? Answer NO only if it shows something else entirely -- a blank panel, printed text, or an unrelated picture. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_notext: Does this image have any printed number, digit, numeral, written label or caption anywhere on it (as opposed to being purely a drawing with no text)? Answer yes if you can see ANY printed number or word, no if there is none. Answer yes or no only.

steps.target: solid round dot that lines run to

steps.read_crop: This close-up is centred on one solid round dot in a drawing where dots are joined by straight lines. Write down every straight line that touches that centre dot, each with a few plain words saying which way it leaves the dot. Write each straight line once. Separate one item from the next with a semicolon; write no running total and nothing else. If there is no solid round dot at the centre of this close-up, write the single word NONE. If there is a centre dot but no straight line touches it, write the single word ZERO.
